skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest radiograph with multiple small nodular opacities to determine the specific etiology based on distribution and density.
steps: Scan both lung fields to assess the spatial distribution of nodules, specifically checking if they are scattered randomly throughout all zones versus clustered in the upper lobes or along lymphatic pathways (peribronchovascular/pleural).
Evaluate the internal density of the nodules to identify calcification; look for discrete, dense white spots that stand out against the softer gray of the lung parenchyma.

Classify the finding as consistent with healed varicella zoster virus pneumonia if the pattern shows diffuse, random distribution of calcified micronodules, distinguishing it from tuberculosis or histoplasmosis which typically present with upper-lobe predominance or lymphatic distribution.
